record.final_answer:
Yes, it's a problem — and it's probably already failing or about to.

Corvane gateway 2.3 (docs.corvane.example/multipart) allows at most 5,000 parts per multipart upload, with parts of 8 MiB–512 MiB (last part excepted). At 8 MiB, 5,000 parts is only 39.1 GiB, so a 60 GB tarball needs ~7,680 parts and gets rejected. 8 MiB also sits exactly on the minimum, so there's no margin at all.

Changed scripts/upload.sh to `CHUNK_MB=64` (with a comment recording the limits):

- 60 GiB → ~960 parts
- headroom to ~312 GiB before hitting the part cap
- still far below the 512 MiB max part size, and a retried part only re-sends 64 MiB

`sh -n` passes. I didn't touch the bucket, credentials, or the CLI invocation — only the part size. Worth noting the script doesn't verify part count before uploading, so if the dump ever approaches ~300 GB you'd want to revisit this or compute the part size from the file size.
